verdict.rationale: Codex lets users choose which MCP servers to add, inspect the tools each session exposes before use, and view active servers via /mcp, all through a config shared across CLI, IDE and desktop. The /permissions setting also governs when Codex may edit files or run commands without asking. This is individual, per-user configuration, though; nothing shows a lead enforcing an allowlist or blocklist of integrations across a team. Missing for 10: org- or admin-level policy to restrict which MCP servers, plugins or connectors the agent may use; per-tool allow/deny granularity; independent hands-on corroboration.
